issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int) as returning void, but the solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) to return boolean. This return-type mismatch is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected method signature and may cause tests or example code to fail if they follow the UML/specification or the solution inconsistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addGuestStudents(int) method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution implementation to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and perform the addition without returning a value, matching the UML/problem statement, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to specify a boolean return type and document the semantics (e.g., return true on success, false on invalid input). Preference: adopt (A) to match the UML as presented.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies addGuestStudents(int): void, but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) returning boolean. This signature mismatch (same method name but different return type/behavior) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement (a void mutator that adds guest students) to the provided solution (which returns a success flag). It may cause test or implementation mismatches since the UML and textual spec indicate no return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either change the solution to implement public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (performing the update and handling invalid input without returning a boolean), or update the problem/UML to indicate a boolean return type and document the success/failure semantics. Prefer changing the solution to void to match the UML and textual description.
